research_input.startup: STARTUP.md chapter 37 (stage 3, month 19): transcripts 6 hours late and nobody alerted; the bank asks who changed a security group last Tuesday. Needs: alarms on waiting work, all logs in one place, a record of every API call for 7 years. Adds CloudWatch metrics, alarms, Logs and dashboards; a CloudTrail organization trail; X-Ray; SNS topic ops-alerts. Options: log files and a weekly review / Prometheus and Grafana on EC2 / CloudWatch, CloudTrail and X-Ray (chosen). Accepts: log volume becomes a cost; alarms need tuning. Chen asks: CloudWatch or CloudTrail, which tells me who changed the security group? Managed Grafana and Managed Service for Prometheus are in the A8 'no workload' list: cards only, never in the story. Story numbers (6 hours, 7 years) are story data, never facts.

Logging guidance from the Security Pillar: SEC04-BP01 configure service and application logging, SEC04-BP02 capture logs, findings and metrics in standardized locations (central log archive account, retention, protection). One or two 'AWS recommends' facts that tie CloudTrail and CloudWatch Logs to compliance.

Facts behind Callvale's decision (CloudWatch, CloudTrail and X-Ray; log files with a weekly review and Prometheus and Grafana on EC2 weighed): (a) alarm on waiting work: an alarm on the queue's age-of-oldest-message metric with an SNS action; (b) all logs in one place: the agent sends logs to log groups, retention per log group, Logs Insights to search; (c) who changed the security group: CloudTrail event history (90 days of management events) and the organization trail for the long record; (d) every API call for 7 years: trail log files in S3 kept as long as needed with Object Lock; (e) X-Ray traces show where the pipeline waits; (f) the trade-offs: log ingestion and storage are priced per GB; alarms need tuning (datapoints to alarm, missing data); self-run Prometheus and Grafana on EC2 means servers to run.
